questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted an English-speaking country and I have always wanted to go to Australia

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. I had a few issues but I emailed UWA and they were very helpful! KU was not the best but that is just typical KU

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I swapped a few units and they helped with that. That was no problem.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Before I arrived, it was my understanding that it would be easy to find a room in Perth. However, it turned out to be rather tricky. I was lucky to find a room in a share-house with two Australians, which improved my stay. Many people lived with other internationals and had a hard time meeting locals but because my roommates were from Perth I got the whole experience. Moreover, my room was pretty cheap. I know that many people had to pay quite a lot for their place. I arrived two weeks before the start of uni and stayed in a hostel. I found a room after two weeks. I think people panicked a bit if they arrived too late and did not have a place to live. So if you can live with the uncertainty for a few weeks, I would recommend finding a once share-house.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is worth it if you have good roommates. I am sure everyone was satisfied with their housing. It all depends on what you want out of it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: pretty easy

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just choose the units you want. This is done on their website. However, because I accidentally saved before actually choosing any units, the page was locked. I had to email UWA to let them know what units I wanted. It was easy but still a bit annoying.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the units I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find units that sound interesting. You can always change once you are at uni. This must be done during the first week but they tell you that. Many other internationals recommended one of my units, so it is worth talking to other people about your choices.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was interesting to try something other than KU. However, you have to do a lot of quizzes, assignments and so on during the semester which means that you do not have the same freedom as at KU.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only chose first-year courses and electives. They were all easy except for my phycology unit. But that was due to the fact that I have never done a lab report. I struggled a bit with the scientific aspect of that unit.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They value participation more and you are marked on the basis of that. "Introduction to Indigenous Heritage and Knowledge" was different from the other units because they wanted the seminars to be like a conversation. But that was interesting to try. The last half of "Cultures, New Media, and Communications" was online. I did not particularly like that aspect because it meant that we had to write on a discussion board inline several times a week.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Active Leadership (SSEH1104)
Boodjar Moort Katitjin: Introduction to Indigenous Heritage and Knowledge (INDG1160)
Cultures, New Media, and Communications (COMM 1002)
Psychology: Behaviour in Context (PSYC1102)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Active Leadership and Boodjar Moort Katitjin: Introduction to Indigenous Heritage and Knowledge were good. They did not require much work which is perfect when you are on exchange. And they were interesting. In active leadership, you have to choose between kayaking, stand-up paddling and mountain biking. You then learn about leadership in relation to the chosen activity.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really any

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is expensive. Fruit, vegetables, and meat from the supermarket are expensive. And alcohol is so expensive. I drank a lot of beer and you can easily pay 80-100 for a six-pack. Public transportation is cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I spent a lot of time with my roommates and I did not feel the need to join any clubs. Moreover, because people at uni are very young, I felt a bit too old for many of the clubs. International students hang out a lot so you do not necessarily need the clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I joined the gym which was nice.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on the trips that uni arranges. You can meet many people through that.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on small trips with your new friends. I did not do that much but I enjoyed my weekends in Perth hanging out with my roommates. There is a study break in September where many people went north to Exmouth or Karijini National Park. I went with a group to Exmouth which was fun. However, I mostly did it because I had fomo. I was not really in the mood for a trip so maybe consider that. After the semester, me and a friend from uni went on a road trip down South all the way to Esperance and spent 6 weeks doing that. I preferred to go on a big road trip in the end and then spent most of my time in Perth and close around, but everyone is different.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Everyone is so friendly and inclusive

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do what you want to do. If you find yourself in a group of people that feels off, go find some other people. There are many internationals and you can easily find your kind of people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They drink a lot! And they go hard when they party.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness. And the inclusiveness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Do what you want to do. Do not feel pressured to do what other people do. Do it at your own pace. Other than that, just enjoy your time and see this as an opportunity to experience a different life and meet new people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Housing is expensive and a challenge. Beer is ridiculously expensive.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting my roommates and the group of international students that I ended up becoming friends with.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not really any challenges. When I arrived, I was a bit stressed and anxious about the housing situation but it worked out well. And if you have a partner at home, it can be hard, if you are not in a good and healthy relationship.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
Enjoy your time. And make it your own. 
And it is pretty cold in Perth. Even at the end of October and November. Colder than you think. Bring jeans, long-sleeved shirts and jackets. The houses are not good in the winter and it can be pretty cold inside.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
